title: Local comparison of parabolics from the closed-fibre Lie algebras
statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with residue field $k$, and let $G$ be a smooth affine finitely presented group scheme over $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Suppose its geometric fibres are connected reductive groups, meaning that they have no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup; unipotent means that all geometric points act by unipotent matrices in a faithful representation. Let $P,Q\subseteq G$ be smooth closed subgroup schemes whose geometric fibres are parabolic subgroups, meaning smooth connected subgroups containing a Borel subgroup; a Borel is a maximal smooth connected solvable subgroup, and solvable means that successive derived subgroups become trivial. Suppose $P$ and $Q$ contain a common split torus $T\simeq\mathbf G_{m,S}^r$ whose geometric fibres are maximal tori of $G$, with $\mathbf G_m(C)=C^\times$. Regard the tangent Lie algebras of their closed fibres as subspaces of $\operatorname{Lie}(G_k)$; the tangent space is the kernel of reduction from dual-number points at the identity. If $\operatorname{Lie}(Q_k)\subseteq\operatorname{Lie}(P_k)$, then $Q\subseteq P$ as closed subgroup schemes of $G$. In particular equality of these Lie algebras implies $P=Q$. When P and Q are Borel subgroup schemes containing T, equality of the sets of nonzero T-weights in their closed-fibre tangent spaces implies P=Q; in this case their zero-weight tangent summands are both Lie(T_k), and each occurring nonzero root summand is the corresponding one-dimensional root space of Lie(G_k).

source.place: Corollary 5.2.7(2), printed pp.155--156, specialized to a local base: every open neighborhood of the closed point is the whole base. Local copy WANTED; primary source read online.

proof.text: The closed subgroups $P,Q$ are affine and finitely presented over $A$: a closed subscheme of the affine $G$ is a quotient of its finitely presented coordinate algebra, and that algebra is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], so the defining ideals are finitely generated. Choose $\lambda:\mathbf G_m\to T$ describing $P$ by [lem-sfb-local-parabolic-cocharacter-description]. Its use is valid for the given split torus and the stated geometric parabolic fibres. Regard conjugation by $\lambda$ as an action on both $G$ and $Q$; it preserves $Q$ since $T\subseteq Q$.

Write $\mathfrak g,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q$ for the tangent modules. By [lem-sfb-relative-tangent-weight-base-change] they are finite projective, have finite character-weight decompositions for the full $T$-coaction, and their weights commute with reduction to $k$. Coarsen the character grading along $\lambda$ to integer weights: $\mathfrak q_j=\bigoplus_{\langle m,\lambda\rangle=j}\mathfrak q_m$, and similarly for $\mathfrak g,\mathfrak p$. Each is finite projective. The inclusions on tangent modules, including after reduction, are injective: a closed subgroup is a subfunctor on every dual-number algebra. These maps preserve weights because the subgroup inclusions commute with conjugation. The tangent formula in [lem-sfb-relative-dynamic-subgroups] gives $\mathfrak p=\bigoplus_{j\geq0}\mathfrak g_j$.

The assumed inclusion on closed-fibre tangent spaces now forces $\mathfrak q_j\otimes_A k=0$ for every $j<0$: its image lies both in the $j$-summand of $\operatorname{Lie}(G_k)$ and in the sum of the nonnegative summands. Every $\mathfrak q_j$ is finite, so [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators], with the empty generating family, gives $\mathfrak q_j=0$. Hence $\mathfrak q$ has only nonnegative $\lambda$-weights over $A$, and therefore after every base change.

source.place: Corollary 5.2.7(2), p.155; explicit local-module version of the root-weight comparison

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relative-dynamic-subgroups] to the action on $Q$, and let $R=P_Q(\lambda)\subseteq Q$. It is smooth, affine, finitely presented, has connected geometric fibres, and its tangent module is the nonnegative part of $\mathfrak q$, which step 3 shows is all of $\mathfrak q$. These properties and tangent identifications commute with arbitrary base change. Over any algebraically closed $A$-field $F$, apply [lem-sfb-smooth-subgroup-tangent-generation] to the smooth connected group $Q_F$, the singleton family $R_F$, and the closed subgroup $K=R_F$. Its tangent image spans $\operatorname{Lie}(Q_F)$, so $R_F=Q_F$. Now [lem-sfb-flat-geometric-fibre-open-criterion] gives $R\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$. The schemes are smooth over $A$; the closed immersion is finitely presented because both coordinate algebras are finite type over the Noetherian ring $A$.

source.place: Corollary 5.2.7(2), p.155: P_Q(lambda) has full Lie algebra; fibrewise step made explicit

proof.text: For every $A$-algebra $B$, an element of $Q(B)=P_Q(\lambda)(B)$ has its conjugation orbit extended to $\operatorname{Spec}B[t]\to Q_B$. Composing this extension with $Q_B\hookrightarrow G_B$ proves that it belongs to $P_G(\lambda)(B)=P(B)$. This proves $Q\subseteq P$ as subgroup functors and hence as closed subgroup schemes. If the two closed-fibre Lie algebras are equal, repeat steps 1--5 with $P,Q$ exchanged. Both subgroup inclusions hold, and thus $P=Q$.

source.place: Corollary 5.2.7(2), p.155, final functorial inclusion and symmetric equality consequence

proof.text: For the additional Borel assertion, extend $k$ to an algebraic closure $F$. The tangent base-change isomorphisms of [lem-sfb-affine-group-lie-tangent-calculus] are natural for inclusions and conjugation. Weight spaces commute with this extension by [lem-sfb-relative-tangent-weight-base-change], applied over the field $k$. By [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description], the tangent space of each of the Borels $P_F,Q_F$ is $\operatorname{Lie}(T_F)$ plus its positive root spaces. By [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections], the zero-weight space of $\operatorname{Lie}(G_F)$ is $\operatorname{Lie}(T_F)$ and every nonzero root space is one-dimensional. Thus each occurring weight space of a Borel is the whole ambient root space. These equalities descend to $k$: for an inclusion of finite-dimensional spaces, extend a basis of the smaller space to one of the larger; a nonzero quotient basis remains nonzero after tensoring with $F$. The zero summands of both Borels are consequently $\operatorname{Lie}(T_k)$, and each occurring nonzero summand is the same ambient one-dimensional root space. Equality of their sets of nonzero character weights gives equality of their direct-sum tangent subspaces; the equality consequence of step 5 yields $P=Q$. This uses full torus characters, not their differentials or just their values on $T(k)$.

source.place: Corollary 5.2.7(2), p.155, Borel consequence; classical tangent descriptions in Sections 1 and 4

New node (Conrad Prop. 5.2.3 on a local base, i.e. a relative parabolic H ⊇ split maximal T equals P_G(λ)): the statement is true. Over the local ring the root set is constant because the weight summands are free. Field case checked in Milne iAG2017 Ch. 21. Edge cases H=G with λ=0, empty root system, nonreduced A and GL_2 all hold. It is self-contained and not a clause of the item. Steps: (1) Noetherian finite presentation; λ for P; conjugation by λ preserves Q since T ⊆ Q. (2) tangent-weight-base-change applied to G, P, Q; coarsening along λ is elementary; Lie(P) = ⊕_{j≥0} 𝔤_j from relative-dynamic-subgroups. (3) Negative weights vanish on the closed fibre, then Nakayama with N=0; correctly marked elementary. (4) P_Q(λ) is smooth with tangent module all of 𝔮; tangent-generation gives R_F=Q_F; the fibre criterion applies (smooth source, finite-type target, finitely presented closed immersion). (5) Composing the extended orbit gives Q ⊆ P; the equality clause follows by symmetry. (6) Borel clause: field extension, regular-cocharacter Borel tangent formula and rank-one reflections give Lie_0 = Lie(T) and one-dimensional root spaces; descent by dimension; uses characters, not differentials. No cycle; cited nodes are in the same unit or are Mathlib leaves.
